body.statement: The chart in Theorem 2 is nonempty in the legal probability model: with \((a,b,c,d)=(1/3,1/2,1/4,1/5)\) and five independent centered unit-rate exponential sources \(S_1,S_2,S_3,S_{12},S_{23}\), the disturbances \(\varepsilon_1=S_1+S_{12}\), \(\varepsilon_2=S_2+S_{12}+S_{23}\), and \(\varepsilon_3=S_3+S_{23}\) define a mechanism \(m\in\mathcal M_3\) whose induced law satisfies \(D(P_m)\neq0\) and whose residual Jacobian \(J_m\) has rank two.
body.justification: A legal witness prevents the algebraic chart from being nonempty only in a formal moment space with no compatible distributions.
body.gap: The general cumulant-transfer obstruction and prior lower-order examples show that formal tensor coordinates need not be probability-realizable.
body.consumer: The witness seeds exact regression tests and supplies a nonvacuous neighborhood for the uniform-inference class.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(E_1,E_2,E_3,E_{12},E_{23}\) be independent unit-rate exponential variables and put \(S_j=E_j-1\). Then \(E[S_j]=0\), \(\kappa_2(S_j)=1\), \(\kappa_3(S_j)=2\), and every moment exists. With the loadings in the statement,
\[
\Omega=
\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&3&1\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Delta=1-\frac16-\frac1{20}=\frac{47}{60}\neq0.
\]
The four structural coefficients are nonzero, the disturbances are centered with finite third moments, and the endpoints depend on disjoint source sets and hence are independent. Each marginal disturbance has moment-generating function equal, near zero, to an exponential factor divided by a nonconstant product of linear factors. Such a function has a finite complex pole, whereas a Gaussian moment-generating function is entire; hence every disturbance marginal is non-Gaussian.

We verify independence genericity directly. For a source-loading column \(L_j\), the coefficient of \(S_j\) in \(u^\top\varepsilon\) is \(u^\top L_j\). If \(u^\top\varepsilon\) and \(w^\top\varepsilon\) are independent, their joint moment-generating function factorizes near the origin. After cancellation of the harmless centering exponentials, unique factorization of polynomials in \(s,t\) in
\[
\prod_j\{1-s\,u^\top L_j-t\,w^\top L_j\}^{-1}
=\prod_j\{1-s\,u^\top L_j\}^{-1}
 \prod_j\{1-t\,w^\top L_j\}^{-1}
\]
shows that \((u^\top L_j)(w^\top L_j)=0\) for every source \(j\): a mixed irreducible linear factor cannot occur on the right. The private columns first give \(u_iw_i=0\) for \(i=1,2,3\). For the shared column \(L_{12}=(1,1,0)^\top\), if, for example, \(u_1w_2\neq0\), the private restrictions force \(w_1=u_2=0\), contradicting \((u_1+u_2)(w_1+w_2)=0\). Thus \(u_1w_2=u_2w_1=0\). The same argument for \(L_{23}=(0,1,1)^\top\) gives \(u_2w_3=u_3w_2=0\). This is exactly Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:independence\mbox{-}genericity}\), so the construction is a member of \(\mathcal M_3\).

Exact inversion of \(K\) and contraction of the source cumulants give
\[
\Sigma=\frac1{2209}
\begin{pmatrix}
10228&11790&3768\\
11790&18450&7920\\
3768&7920&6848
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
v=\frac{18450}{2209},
\qquad
\chi=-\frac{10800}{2209}.
\]
Using only these observed second and third cumulants in Definitions \(\mathrm{def:observable\mbox{-}cubics}\) and \(\mathrm{def:subresultant\mbox{-}chart}\) yields
\[
P_3(z)=-\frac{7200}{4879681}(3z-1)(10z-19)(165z-196),
\]
\[
Q_3(z)=-\frac{648000}{229345007}(3z-1)
       (23175z^2-32135z+11082),
\]
and
\[
s_1=\frac{185935386814617600000000000000}
{256666986187667409334369}\neq0,
\qquad
s_0=-\frac{s_1}{3}.
\]
Thus \(v,\chi,p_3,q_3,s_1\) are all nonzero and therefore \(D(P_m)\neq0\). Finally, differentiation of the three observable residual moments with respect to \((\alpha,\delta)\), evaluated at \((1/3,1/5)\), gives
\[
J_m=
\begin{pmatrix}
-90/47&-120/47\\
0&-240/47\\
-180/47&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its second and third rows are linearly independent, so \(\operatorname{rank}(J_m)=2\), completing the legal nonemptiness certificate.
